articles.title: Drone Strikes Cripple Half of Russia's Top Diesel Refineries
articles.description: Three of Russia's six largest diesel-producing refineries are now either shut or operating at roughly one-quarter capacity after Ukrainian drone attacks damaged plants that together form the backbone of the country's fuel system. The six refineries—Omsk, Kirishi, Taneco, Volgograd, NORSI and Perm—account for roughly half of Russia's diesel production, according to Reuters calculations based on market data. articles.description: A new fiscal regime in the UK from 2027 could deliver an additional £14.9 billion, or $20 billion, to Britain’s revenues, the leading offshore industry group said in its annual Economic Report, calling on the Burnham government to bring forward the tax change planned for 2030. Offshore Energies UK (OEUK) wants the Oil and Gas Revenue Levy, a price-triggered mechanism planned to replace the current Energy Profits Levy from 2030, to be introduced from January 2027. articles.description: Depressed LNG demand in recent months in China and India is the result of spiking LNG prices due to the Middle East conflict, and consumption in the key Asian gas import markets is set to rebound once the war ends and prices normalize, industry executives say. articles.description: Last week’s drone attacks on Saudi Arabia’s key East-West oil pipeline have caused damage that could take weeks to repair, potentially significantly cutting the disrupted crude oil flows from the Middle East. Saudi Arabia was forced to temporarily shut down the East-West oil pipeline following drone attacks launched from the territory of Iraq close to the Iranian border on Thursday. articles.title: Global Fuel Squeeze Triggers U.S. Refiners Stocks Rally
articles.description: Energy stocks have rallied this year as oil prices soared amid the Middle East conflict.
